summary: Players secretly back one of several rival claimants to a divided kingdom and spend a tight hand of dual-use cards to reinforce armies in contested regions or squirrel away resources for later. At the end, whichever faction actually ends up strongest on the map determines who scores well, so a lot of the game is reading opponents' hidden loyalties and nudging the map toward (or away from) outcomes that favor you.
praised: tight, elegant ruleset for the depth it produces
criticised: can feel swingy or kingmaker-y when one player is clearly losing
some find the theme thin dressing over an abstract system

interaction.kind: area majority and influence on a shared map
interaction.detail: Players commit hidden influence cards to the same regions on a shared map of the divided kingdom, and gaining majority in a region comes directly at the expense of rivals who committed there too. There is no direct attack or shared resource market; the contest is entirely about out-maneuvering others for control of common territory.

scoring.how_you_win: Players secretly place influence to help one of three factions gain control of contested regions; when the map resolves, you win if the faction you backed (kept secret via hidden agenda) ends up dominant, not by accumulating points.

_name: The King Is Dead: Second Edition
